U0400.d: U0400 is the unspecific entry of the invalid-data block. It says that a module receives messages from another node on time but rejects their content, without naming the sender; the codes from U0401 upward name the partner.
s: Code cannot be cleared or returns at once
Functions of the storing module limited or warning lamp on, depending on the vehicle
c: Modules on different software levels after a partial update
Replaced module not programmed or configured
Disturbed bus signal from poor connections or low supply voltage

U0401.d: U0401 is stored by a module that keeps receiving the engine or powertrain controller's messages but finds their content faulty. Most often the transmission controller logs it; Ford's 2012 OBD summary names engine torque and pedal position as the data concerned.
s: Check engine light, often stored in the transmission controller
Harsh shifts or transmission limp-home mode
Adaptive cruise control switched off
c: Software of the ECM/PCM or of the receiving module (update available)
ECM sends a signal flagged invalid, for example after its own sensor fault
Disturbed CAN traffic from connectors, wiring or low battery voltage

U0402.d: U0402 is the reverse case of U0401: the engine controller or another listener receives the transmission controller's frames but rejects their content. GM's 2025 ECM checks counter, protection value and checksum of the estimated-gear and general transmission information signals, flags a fault at 8 errors among 18 checks, Type A after one trip; the body controller uses 15 of 16 and Type B.
s: Check engine light
Transmission stuck in a fixed gear (limp mode)
Harsh or delayed shifts
c: Software of PCM or TCM (update available)
Internal transmission fault making the TCM send implausible values
Disturbed CAN traffic from connectors, wiring or low voltage

U0403.d: U0403 points to data from the transfer case control module, the unit that engages four-wheel drive and selects the range: its frames keep coming, yet the listener rejects what they carry. In GM's 2025 tables the ECM watches the secondary-axle signals from this module for faulty rolling counter, protection value or checksum, needs 8 bad results out of 18 to fail and assigns Type B (MIL on the second trip), whereas the
s: Service 4WD message
Traction control or check engine light on
Driveline bumps or clicking from the transfer case motor
c: Software of the transfer case or drivetrain control module (update available)
Ignition voltage dropping out at fuse block terminals or relays
Faulty range position sensor making the module send implausible values
Transfer case control module internally faulty

U0404.d: Gear shift control module A is the electronic selector of shift-by-wire cars: lever, dial or buttons that report the chosen range as data. U0404 means its messages still arrive but the receiver, usually the transmission controller, rejects them.
s: Selector fault message or flashing range indicator
Range cannot be selected or vehicle stays in Park
Check engine light
c: Software of TCM or gateway (update available)
Position sensor or electronics in the selector delivering implausible values
Connector or bus line at the selector loose or corroded

U0405.d: Today the module behind this code is usually the distance radar of adaptive cruise, the unit that asks the engine controller for speed and torque changes. U0405 is set when those requests arrive but fail the receiver's integrity checks.
s: Adaptive cruise control unavailable
Check engine light that does not go out after clearing
c: Engine controller software detecting the fault falsely (update available)
Radar or cruise module sending implausible requests, for example after misalignment or damage
Disturbed CAN traffic from connectors or wiring

U0406.d: U0406 means a receiving controller, normally the ECM/PCM, gets messages from the fuel injector control module that arrive but fail its checks: wrong counter, checksum, range or a signal marked invalid. Ford's 2012 OBD summary shows the U04xx principle with U0401: the TCM stores it when the ECM sends invalid or faulted torque or pedal data.
s: Check engine light on
Rough running, misfire or hard start
Reduced power
c: Corroded or loose connector, damaged bus wire to the injector module
Low supply voltage at the injector module
Software levels of injector module and ECM do not match

U0407.d: U0407 is stored when the engine controller receives data from the glow plug control module that it rejects as implausible. Volkswagen lists the code in the 2014 Touareg diesel OBD chart as Invalid Data Received From Glow Plug Control Module 1, criterion implausible messages received.
s: Check engine or glow plug light on
Hard starting in cold weather
White smoke and rough idle after cold start
c: LIN wire or connector between glow module and ECM corroded or loose
Glow plug control module internally faulty
Voltage dip during glow check or cranking
Glow module software does not match the ECM

U0408.d: U0408 points to messages from the throttle actuator control module that the receiver, usually the ECM/PCM, judges invalid: implausible content, a failed checksum or counter, or a value outside its range. Most vehicles integrate throttle control in the engine controller, so a separate TAC module and therefore this code are uncommon; no manufacturer documents U0408 publicly.
s: Check engine light on
Limp mode with reduced throttle response
Unstable idle or stalling
c: Damaged bus wire or poor connector contact at the throttle module
Throttle actuator control module internally faulty
Software of throttle module and ECM do not match

U0409.d: U0409 is logged when the engine controller receives data from the alternative fuel control module that fail its validity checks. Such a module runs the gas side of bi-fuel CNG or LPG vehicles.
s: Check engine light on
Engine stays on or switches back to petrol
Gas gauge or fuel mode indicator incorrect
c: Corroded connector or damaged wiring of the retrofit or factory gas system
Faulty gas rail pressure/temperature sensor delivering implausible values
Alternative fuel control module faulty or wrongly configured

U040A.d: J2012 separates the air conditioning control module, which governs the refrigerant side with compressor, pressures and, in electrified cars, an electric compressor drive, from the HVAC module that handles blower, flaps and set temperature (invalid data from that one is U0424). U040A is stored when frames from the A/C unit arrive but carry values the receiver cannot trust, such as a failed counter or checksum or a sig
s: Air conditioning blows warm, compressor stays off
Windows demist slowly
c: Software of the A/C control module or of the receiver out of step
Faulty pressure or temperature input making the module send invalid values
Disturbed bus line, poor ground or low supply voltage at the module

U040B.d: U040B refers to an exhaust gas recirculation system driven by its own electronics on the bus, for example a smart EGR valve actuator that receives position targets and returns its measured position. The code is set when that unit's replies reach the engine controller but fail plausibility or protection checks, so the controller can no longer verify how much exhaust gas flows back.
s: Check engine light
Reduced power or rough idle
EGR flow codes stored alongside
c: Electronics or position sensor of the EGR actuator A delivering implausible values
Heat-damaged connector or bus line at the EGR unit
Software of engine controller and EGR module A out of step
EGR control module A internally faulty

U040C.d: U040C concerns a second, separately networked EGR control unit, B. Two units appear on engines with separate high- and low-pressure recirculation paths, common on modern diesels, or with one EGR valve per cylinder bank; which one counts as B is up to the maker.
s: Check engine light
Reduced power, more smoke or higher fuel consumption
c: Electronics or position sensor of EGR actuator B delivering implausible values
Connector or bus line in the branch of module B damaged by heat or moisture
Module B with software that does not match the engine controller

U040D.d: Turbocharger/supercharger control module A is in practice an electronic charger actuator that sets the vanes of a variable-geometry turbine or a wastegate on command and reports position and status back. U040D means those reports arrive but the engine controller judges them invalid.
s: Check engine light
Noticeably reduced power (limp mode)
Boost pressure codes stored alongside
c: Electronics of the turbo actuator degraded by heat
Sticking vanes or linkage making the actuator report implausible positions
Connector or sensor bus line at the actuator damaged

U040E.d: U040E is reserved for a second charger control module, B, on engines that run two separately actuated chargers: twin or sequential turbo layouts, or a turbocharger combined with an electrically driven or clutched supercharger. The engine controller sets it when module B's position or status messages keep coming but are judged invalid.
s: Check engine light
Reduced power, especially at higher load
c: Electronics or position feedback of charger actuator B faulty
Connector or bus line of module B damaged by heat
Module B with software that does not match the engine controller

U040F.d: On a diesel with SCR, the reductant control module looks after the urea circuit, chiefly the pump, dosing and heater control, and reports pressure and status to the engine controller. U040F means its messages arrive but fail validation.
s: Check engine light
DEF/AdBlue warning with countdown to a speed limit
Further SCR or reductant pump codes stored
c: Pump motor controller in the reductant module reporting an invalid control signal
Corroded connector or damaged bus line at the tank-mounted module
Software of the reductant module or ECM out of step

U0410.d: U0410 means the engine controller receives data from the fuel pump control module that it cannot trust, such as a bad checksum, counter or an out-of-range value. Many cars drive the in-tank pump through such a module to set the low-side pressure on demand.
s: Check engine light on
Fuel pressure codes such as P2635 set together
Hesitation, stalling or reduced power
c: Damaged bus wire or corroded connector to the fuel pump module (often near the tank)
Poor power or ground of the fuel pump module
Pump module and ECM software do not match after replacement
Fuel pump control module internally faulty

U0411.d: U0411 is stored when a controller, typically the engine or hybrid controller, receives messages from the drive motor control module (the inverter electronics of an electric traction motor) that it judges invalid. Volkswagen lists it in its 2014 hybrid OBD charts: for the Touareg Hybrid on implausible messages from the motor module, for the Jetta Hybrid on an incorrect CAN data length code.
s: Engine or drive system warning light on
Electric drive unavailable, engine runs constantly
Reduced power
c: Damaged pins or poor contact in harness connectors near the drive motor (Bentley case)
Faulty motor temperature sensor circuit making the module send invalid data
Software of motor module and hybrid controller do not match
Drive motor control module internally faulty

U0412.d: U0412 is stored when the hybrid or engine controller receives data from battery energy control module A, the management unit of the high-voltage battery, that it rejects as invalid. Volkswagen's 2014 Jetta Hybrid OBD chart sets it on implausible received data.
s: Check engine light on, code may become permanent
Charging or electric driving limited
Hybrid system warning message
c: Software error in hybrid controller or battery management (FCA: reflash HCP/AHCP)
Bus wiring or connector fault between battery module and hybrid controller
Weak 12 V battery disturbing module start-up
Battery energy control module internally faulty

U0413.d: U0413 is the counterpart of U0412 for battery energy control module B, used where the high-voltage battery has a second management unit or a split controller. Volkswagen's 2014 Jetta Hybrid chart sets it on implausible data, while the 2014 Touareg Hybrid chart uses U0413 for its single battery module, which shows that the A/B assignment is maker-specific.
s: Drive system or engine warning light on
Electric driving or charging restricted
Code stored in engine and electric drive controllers
c: Software error in battery management or junction box (Audi: SVM update)
Bus wiring or connector fault at the battery module
Battery energy control module B internally faulty

U0414.d: U0414 is set when a listener, usually the engine controller, receives frames from the four-wheel-drive clutch control module but cannot trust what they carry. That module regulates an on-demand coupling feeding torque to the secondary axle and reports its state on the bus.
s: AWD or 4WD warning in the cluster
Drive on the primary axle only
Check engine light after two trips
c: Four-wheel-drive clutch module sends faulty values (internal fault, moisture)
Disturbed CAN traffic from connectors, wiring or low supply voltage
Clutch module and receiver on software levels that do not match

U0415.d: U0415 means a module accepts frames from the ABS control module only to find their content invalid, typically wheel speeds or brake status with a wrong counter, checksum or a value flagged as unavailable. GM's Saab 9-5 list (2011) splits it into sub-types 72 (message counter) and 74 (checksum) for the electronic brake module.
s: ABS, traction or stability warning lamps
Check engine light and Service Transmission message (model-specific)
AWD, steering or camera functions limited
c: Software of the receiving module (TCM, AWD, steering) too strict or faulty; update available
ABS module passing on implausible values, for example from a faulty wheel speed sensor
Disturbed CAN traffic from water in connectors, wiring or low voltage

U0416.d: U0416 points at the vehicle dynamics control module, the stability control unit that brakes single wheels and trims engine torque. A receiver logs the code when that unit's frames arrive but fail the plausibility check.
s: Adaptive cruise or emergency brake assist unavailable
Stability or brake warning in the cluster
c: Weak or recently disconnected 12 V battery disturbing the stability unit's data
Software of the receiving assistance module (radar, camera) needs an update
Steering angle or sensor calibration lost after battery work
Missing or damaged wire or connector in the bus branch

U0417.d: U0417 covers implausible data from the park brake control module, the controller of an electric parking brake that clamps the rear calipers by motor and reports apply state and faults on the bus. A receiver stores it when these frames arrive with a bad counter, checksum or an invalid value.
s: Park brake warning lamp or message
Auto hold or hill start assist unavailable
Code only stored in history without current fault
c: Low battery voltage or a voltage dip corrupting park brake messages
Park brake control module or its actuator feedback faulty
Connector or wiring fault in the park brake bus branch

U0418.d: U0418 says a node rejects the content of frames from brake system control module A, on many cars the unit that combines ABS, stability control and brake boost. GM's 2025 tables are detailed: the engine controller tests brake status signals for bad counters, protection values or checksums, 8 faults in 18 checks give Type A with MIL after one trip; the TCM runs the same test as Type B, the BCM demands 15 bad of 16, and
s: Check engine light
Adaptive cruise, stop-start or driver assistance unavailable
Brake or stability warning in the cluster
c: Low battery voltage (below about 10 V) during start or standstill
Engine or transmission controller software reacting too sensitively; update available
Loose connector or harness fault disturbing the chassis bus
Brake system control module internally faulty

U0419.d: U0419 concerns the steering effort control module, which varies the assistance or steering ratio the driver feels. Ford uses that name for the controller of its adaptive steering: bulletin 16-2066 on the 2016 Edge and MKX stores C1B00 in the steering effort control module (SECM) and replaces the steering wheel that houses the actuator.
s: Steering system warning in the cluster
Steering ratio or assistance no longer speed-dependent
c: Steering effort module or its actuator reporting implausible values
Clock spring, connector or bus wiring fault in the steering branch
Module not calibrated or configured after replacement

U041A.d: U041A refers to the battery isolation or voltage stabilization module, which separates an auxiliary battery or sensitive loads from the starter circuit, so a restart after an automatic engine stop leaves the rest of the electrical system at stable voltage. GM's patent US 9,803,608 builds such an isolator from MOSFET switches.
s: Automatic stop-start not available
Battery or charging system message
c: Poor ground connection of the isolation module
Weak auxiliary battery making the module report implausible values
Battery isolator or stabilizer internally faulty

U041B.d: U041B names exhaust gas sensor module A, an electronic unit that heats and evaluates an exhaust probe, usually a wide-band oxygen sensor, and sends the result as bus data. The engine controller sets the code when the module still talks but its values fail plausibility, carry wrong counters or report the sensor as not ready.
s: Check engine light
Higher fuel use or regeneration problems on diesels
c: Heat-damaged sensor harness or connector at the sensor module
Aged or contaminated probe giving implausible readings
Exhaust gas sensor module internally faulty

U041C.d: U041C relates to rocker arm control module A, the controller that switches oil-actuated rocker arms to change valve lift or shut cylinders down. The engine controller stores it when the module's lock-state or feedback frames arrive with implausible content, wrong counters or invalid values.
s: Check engine light
Cylinder deactivation or valve lift switching locked out
Higher fuel consumption
c: Low oil pressure or sticking switching solenoid causing implausible lock-state feedback
Rocker arm control module A internally faulty
Connector or bus wiring fault at module A

U041D.d: U041D is the counterpart for rocker arm control module B, used where the switching of rocker arms is split, for instance by cylinder bank. The code tells that the engine controller still receives B's messages, but their lift or lock status cannot be trusted.
s: Check engine light
Uneven running or higher fuel use
c: Switching solenoid or oil supply on the B side faulty
Rocker arm control module B internally faulty
Shared supply or bus fault (then usually with U041C)

U041E.d: U041E concerns the all-wheel-drive control module, the unit that manages a complete AWD or transfer case system rather than a single clutch (U0414). A receiver logs it when that module's torque, mode or status frames arrive but are invalid.
s: 4WD or AWD service light
Check engine light (model-specific)
Four-wheel-drive modes unavailable
c: Transfer case shift motor or module connector not fully seated
Transfer case motor or position sensor faulty, making the module send invalid status

U041F.d: U041F addresses throttle actuator B control module, a separately housed driver for a second electronic throttle. Most engines use one throttle driven directly by the engine controller; a separate driver for the first throttle is covered by U0408.
s: Check engine light
Reduced power or limp-home mode
c: Position feedback of throttle actuator B implausible (sensor or gearbox wear)
Throttle actuator B control module internally faulty
Connector or bus wiring fault at module B

U0420.d: U0420 is stored when a listener gets frames from power steering control module A, the electric assist unit on rack or column, yet judges their content unusable. GM's 2025 tables name several listeners: the ECM tests the steering wheel information for bad counter, protection value or checksum and needs 8 failures within 18 samples for a Type C fault with no MIL; the EBCM runs similar Type C tests, and the EOCM3 assist
s: Adaptive cruise, lane keeping or emergency braking unavailable
Stability control or steering warning in the cluster
Code returns after cold starts with a weak battery
c: Low battery voltage during cranking corrupts steering module start-up data
Steering module or receiving module software needs an update
Corroded connector or poor ground at the steering module

U0421.d: Suspension control module A runs air springs, ride height or adjustable dampers and broadcasts level and status data. U0421 tells that a receiving module gets these frames but finds them corrupt or implausible.
s: Service air suspension or leveling warning
Ride height no longer adjusts
Stability or brake system message alongside
c: Suspension module software hang, cleared by a power reset
Low supply voltage or weak battery during start-up
Internal fault of the suspension control module

U0422.d: U0422 applies to cars with a single body controller; with several, U0431 names body control module A and U0443 to U0446 modules B to E. A receiver logs it when BCM frames arrive but carry unusable content.
s: Check engine light on some vehicles
Cruise control or driver assistance unavailable
Wrong outside temperature or A/C not working
c: Battery disconnect or low voltage leaves default values in BCM messages
Missing or wrong BCM configuration such as VIN, tire size or vehicle options
BCM or receiver software fault, cured by an update

U0423.d: The instrument cluster does more than display: it sends outside temperature, display and chime status or confirmations from its menus to other units. U0423 marks cluster frames that arrive but fail the receiver's checks.
s: Stability, tire pressure or assistance warnings that cannot be cleared
Adaptive cruise or auto high beam unavailable
Check engine light on some makes
c: Battery, fuse or display disconnected so the cluster sends start values
Software fault in cluster or receiving module
Another node on the same bus disturbing the cluster's messages

U0424.d: The HVAC control module reports climate requests and, on newer layouts, also the voltages of switches on the climate faceplate that it measures itself. U0424 says a receiver rejects these frames.
s: Climate controls or buttons react incorrectly or not at all
A/C or defrost not available
Check engine light on some makes
c: HVAC control module or faceplate electronics faulty
Low battery voltage or a reset of the HVAC module during start-up
HVAC or BCM software level that needs an update

U0425.d: U0425 concerns the auxiliary heater control module, the controller of an extra heat source such as a fuel-fired coolant heater on a diesel. The HVAC or engine controller sets it when the heater's status frames arrive with implausible content.
s: Auxiliary or parking heater does not start
Slow warm-up and weak cabin heat in cold weather
c: Auxiliary heater control unit faulty or locked after an internal fault
Low supply voltage at the heater, for example from a weak battery
Loose terminals or corrosion in the heater's bus connector

U0426.d: The vehicle immobilizer control module reads the transponder in the key and passes a coded release to the engine controller. U0426 is logged when that release or status message arrives but cannot be accepted, so the handshake fails even though the module is still talking.
s: Engine cranks but does not start, or no start at times
Security or key warning lamp flashing
Key hard to remove from the ignition
c: Ignition feed voltages do not match the key position, often due to aftermarket equipment
Damaged key transponder or key not matched to the vehicle

U0427.d: The vehicle security control module looks after theft protection: alarm, door, bonnet and tailgate monitoring and, with some makers, the key authorisation for the engine. U0427 marks messages from this module that reach a partner but fail its checks.
s: Alarm triggers falsely or cannot be armed
Remote locking or keyless functions unreliable
Engine start refused on vehicles where the module joins the key check
c: Security control module faulty or reset during start-up
Aftermarket alarm or remote start interfering with the module or its supply
Poor terminal fit or corrosion at the module connector

U0428.d: U0428 is for a separately networked steering angle sensor module, usually on the column, feeding angle and rate to stability control, assistance and stop-start. GM's 2025 brake module counts wrong checksums or counters in its frames (8 of a 16 window) and reacts at once to a cleared validity bit or a data mask stuck at zero, all Type C without MIL.
s: Stability control or steering warning lamp
Stop-start stops the engine at the wrong moment or stays off
Check engine light on some vehicles
c: Steering angle sensor not calibrated after replacement or alignment work
Software in the engine, brake or steering controller misjudging the sensor data

U0429.d: U0429 covers the steering column control module (SCCM), which reads stalks and wheel buttons and on many cars also houses the steering angle sensor. A partner logs the code when SCCM frames are received but rejected.
s: Steering or power steering warning lamp
Cruise control or stalk functions unavailable
Driver assistance systems switched off
c: Vehicle configuration not restored or aligned after a module repair
Software fault in PCM, steering unit or column module
Steering column control module or its angle sensor faulty

U042A.d: The V2X module is the radio node for vehicle-to-everything messaging with other cars, roadside units and the network, via DSRC/ITS-G5 or cellular C-V2X. U042A tells that another module gets frames from it but cannot use their content.
s: Connected traffic or hazard warnings missing
Message about unavailable connected services
c: V2X module or receiver software fault
V2X module faulty, for example after a supply interruption
Antenna or positioning input problem leading to invalid status data

U042B.d: Chassis control module A is a generic name for a controller that coordinates chassis functions, and the job behind the letter varies by brand. GM's documents give one concrete owner: the 2020 ten-speed transmission controller (20OBDG03A) treats the integrated chassis control module (ICCM) as chassis control module A and watches its frame $1F7; an L20 engine controller of 2016 also listens to this module.
s: Chassis, stability or suspension warning
Chassis functions such as damping or traction aids limited
c: Software fault in the chassis module or the receiving controller
Low voltage or reset of the chassis module during operation

U042C.d: U042C refers to a second chassis controller, labelled B, where chassis tasks are split between two units. It is stored when that module's frames still arrive but carry a bad counter, checksum or implausible values.
s: Chassis or suspension warning in the cluster
Chassis function handled by module B inactive
c: Software fault in chassis module B or the receiver
Supply, ground or gateway problem affecting the module's messages

U042D.d: The active vibration control module drives active engine mounts or inertial actuators that push against engine vibration in counter-phase, useful with cylinder deactivation. It needs engine speed and other data from the bus and reports its own status back.
s: Noticeable vibration or humming at idle
More body vibration when cylinders are deactivated
c: Control unit software not matching replaced mounts or actuators
Low supply voltage or poor connection at the module

U042E.d: U042E points to the regulator of generator A, on many Ford models a smart alternator that the PCM commands over a LIN line and that answers with load, temperature and fault status. The PCM stores U042E when those answers come back distorted or implausible; if they stop altogether, U012D is set instead, and U0284 often joins because grille shutters may share the line.
s: Check charging system message or battery lamp
Battery runs down, starting problems
Grille shutter codes stored at the same time
c: Chafed or shorted LIN wire between PCM and generator
Water intrusion or corrosion in a connector of the LIN circuit
Faulty voltage regulator of the generator

U042F.d: U042F concerns a camshaft position control module, used where an electric motor with its own electronics moves the phaser instead of an oil valve. The engine controller commands a target angle and receives actual position and status; U042F means those replies arrive but fail plausibility or protection checks, while U012E is set when they stop.
s: Check engine light
Reduced power and rougher idle
Higher fuel consumption
c: Electric valve timing control module faulty
Supply, ground or connector fault at the module
Engine controller software misjudging the module data

U0430.d: U0430 means that a receiver gets frames from the tire pressure monitor module but rejects what they contain, such as wheel pressures, sensor identifiers or a system status outside the permitted range, or a broken message counter. A stand-alone evaluation unit exists for example in the 2020 Jeep Gladiator Rubicon, whose TPM module FCA reflashed to add the selectable tire fill alert (bulletin 08-023-20).
s: TPMS malfunction lamp on or flashing
Tire pressures missing or shown as dashes in the cluster
c: Outdated or unsuitable software in the tire pressure module
Wheel sensors not learned after tire or wheel change, module sends default values
Poor supply, ground or connector at the tire pressure module

U0431.d: U0431 points at body control module A on vehicles that split body functions over several controllers; with a single BCM the code is U0422, and units B to E have U0443 to U0446. Mitsubishi documents it in the all-wheel-drive ECU, which reads body data from the ETACS unit, among them the stop light switch, and sets U0431 when that signal is abnormal; CAN lines and ETACS codes are checked before the AWD unit is replaced
s: All-wheel-drive or 4WD warning lamp on
Ignition or comfort functions do not switch on
Further body-related warnings in the cluster
c: Software of the receiving module (e.g. AWD unit) misreads body data, reflash needed
Body control module A software or coding faulty
Supply or ground problem at body control module A

U0432.d: Multi-axis acceleration sensor module A is the inertial unit that reports yaw rate plus lateral and longitudinal acceleration to stability control, airbag and assistance systems. U0432 is logged when its frames arrive but fail integrity tests.
s: Stability control, ABS or AWD warnings
Start-stop or driver assistance functions unavailable
Several chassis codes stored at once
c: Corroded connector or terminals in the sensor module harness
Software in the receiving module (PCM, brake module) needs an update
Internal fault or loose mounting of the inertial sensor module

U0433.d: U0433 concerns the forward distance sensor of adaptive cruise control when there is only one or when it sits in the middle, usually a long-range radar behind the grille. A receiver stores it when the radar's object frames fail their protection checks or carry implausible values.
s: Adaptive cruise control switched off
Forward collision warning or emergency braking unavailable
c: Radar misaligned after front-end work or impact, sending implausible objects
Radar or assistance controller software out of step
Low supply voltage or poor connector at the radar

U0434.d: The active roll control module drives actuators that twist the anti-roll bars on both axles against body lean, hydraulically in older designs and electrically in newer ones. U0434 tells that a receiver, for instance the chassis or brake controller, gets this module's status or torque frames but cannot trust their content.
s: Suspension or chassis warning in the cluster
Noticeably more body roll in corners
c: Roll control module software fails to initialise reliably
Weak supply to the roll control actuators or module
Internal fault of the roll control module or actuator

U0435.d: U0435 refers to the rear power steering module, the controller of active rear-wheel steering. A receiver sets it when the module's status or angle frames arrive but are unusable.
s: Service Soon or rear steering fault message
Larger turning circle, rear wheels held straight
c: Rear steering module not yet ready when receivers expect data, e.g. at remote start
Software error in rear steering or brake module
Low voltage or poor connector at the rear steering unit

U0436.d: U0436 concerns the front differential control module, a controller that locks or meters the front axle differential, for example the electric locker of an off-road vehicle. A receiver records the code when lock status, clutch torque or diagnostic frames from this module look implausible.
s: Front locker or 4WD function unavailable
ABS, stability or drivetrain warning
c: Fault in the locking module electronics, e.g. degraded measuring resistor
Corroded or damaged harness and connector near the front axle

U0437.d: The rear differential control module runs an electronic limited-slip differential or the rear clutch of an on-demand all-wheel drive. U0437 is set when a receiver gets its frames but finds torque, clutch state or counter values invalid.
s: Service AWD or rear axle message
All-wheel drive or limited-slip function inactive
c: Rear differential module software needs reprogramming
Corrosion at the module mounted on or near the rear axle
Faulty clutch actuator or motor feeding implausible status

U0438.d: U0438 names the trailer brake control module, which applies the electric brakes of a towed trailer in step with the vehicle's braking; park brake data has a code of its own, U0417. Ford uses U0438 explicitly: SSM 52184 connects U0438:82 stored by the cluster of some 2023 F-150 PowerBoost hybrids, built from 24 to 26 October 2022, with a Trailer Brake System Fault message caused by the cluster configuration, which is
s: Trailer brake system fault message
Trailer brake gain cannot be set or trailer brakes inactive
Further network warnings in the cluster
c: Loose or wrongly tightened body ground
Internal fault of the trailer brake control module

U0439.d: U0439 relates to the all terrain control module, which manages drive modes for snow, sand, mud or rock and passes the chosen setting to powertrain, brake and suspension controllers. A receiver sets it when mode request, switch state or status frames from this module look invalid.
s: Check 4x4 or terrain system message
Drive mode selection does not respond
c: Terrain or 4WD mode switch stuck or obstructed by trim
All terrain module software or variant coding wrong
Poor supply, ground or connector at the module

U043A.d: Suspension control module B is a second chassis controller, often the one that runs adjustable dampers while module A handles levelling. U043A is logged when its frames reach a receiver but fail integrity checks.
s: Service suspension or ride control warning
Ride noticeably firmer or softer than usual
c: Damper module resets or hangs, sending frozen counters
Low supply voltage at the suspension module
Software of suspension and brake modules not matched

U043B.d: U043B covers the left front distance sensor, usually a short-range corner radar that widens the view of adaptive cruise and collision assistance beyond the central long-range unit; that one has U0433, the right corner U043C. A receiver sets U043B when the left sensor's object or status frames arrive but fail plausibility or protection checks.
s: Adaptive cruise or lane change assistance unavailable
Message to clean or check front sensors
c: Left corner radar misaligned or damaged after a bumper impact
Corner radar software not matching the assistance controller
Moisture or corrosion in the left sensor connector

U043C.d: U043C is the right-hand counterpart: invalid frames from the right front distance sensor, a corner radar on cars that pair one long-range radar with two short-range units. Finding only U043C points at that sensor, its plug or its mounting area, for example after a light knock on the right bumper corner; U043B and U043C together suggest a shared supply, bus segment or a software issue in the receiver.
s: Assistance functions using the right front view switched off
Sensor blocked or check sensor message
c: Right corner radar knocked out of alignment or damaged
Shared supply or bus segment fault when both corner codes appear
Moisture or corrosion in the right sensor connector

U043D.d: U043D applies where the accelerator pedal is a networked module that sends pedal position as messages instead of two analogue voltages. The engine or vehicle controller stores it when those messages carry an implausible position, redundant values that disagree or a broken counter.
s: Reduced power or limp-home mode
Engine or drivetrain warning lamp on
Pedal response delayed or ignored
c: Poor pin contact at the pedal module or its receiver connector
Internal fault of the accelerator pedal module
Pedal module and engine controller software not matched

U043E.d: Vacuum sensor A reports the vacuum in a brake booster or vacuum reservoir; U043E is meant for designs in which this sensor sends digital messages and a receiver judges them invalid. No manufacturer documents U043E publicly.
s: Brake assist warning message
Hard brake pedal or vacuum pump running often
c: Faulty sensor electronics giving wrong vacuum values
Oil or dirt in the sensor, check valve or vacuum hose
Poor terminal tension at the sensor connector

U043F.d: U043F is the counterpart for vacuum sensor B, used where a second vacuum signal exists, for example a redundant booster sensor or one watching a separate reservoir. A receiver records it when B's digital vacuum value arrives invalid.
s: Brake assist or vacuum system warning
Start-stop or other vacuum-dependent functions inactive
c: Faulty vacuum sensor B or its electronics
Damaged wiring branch or connector to sensor B
Actual vacuum leak making both sensors disagree

U0440.d: U0440 points at the pedestrian alert control module, which drives the external speaker of electric and hybrid vehicles. FMVSS 141 in the US demands an audible signal while the vehicle stands with its propulsion active and at speeds below 30 km/h, so the module needs speed, gear and propulsion state and reports its own status back.
s: Pedestrian alert system warning in the cluster
No external sound at low speed
c: Loose or vibrating connector at the alert module
Alert module software not matched to the vehicle
Internal fault of the pedestrian alert module

U0441.d: U0441 does not name one controller: the title refers to emissions-critical control information, the data powertrain units exchange for emission-relevant functions. A receiver logs it when such a message arrives but fails plausibility, counter or checksum tests; if the information stops altogether, U0113 applies.
s: Check engine light on
Additional powertrain or network codes stored
Emissions inspection not passed while the code is present
c: Software of the powertrain unit sending the emission data is outdated or mismatched
Fault in the powertrain CAN wiring or connectors corrupting messages
Low or unstable supply voltage at the sending or receiving unit

U0442.d: ECM/PCM B stands for a second engine or powertrain controller where a car carries more than one such unit; U0442 means its frames reach a receiver with invalid content, while U0115 means they stop arriving. Mazda applies the code in its own way: bulletin 01-015/18 for the 2018 Mazda6 and CX-5 and the 2019 CX-3 and MX-5 describes the TCM of automatic models flagging invalid PCM data, together with P061B and U0401, whe
s: Check engine light on
Fail-safe mode with limited engine speed or lack of power
Transmission codes stored alongside engine codes
c: Control logic in the engine or powertrain software too sensitive, update available
Software levels of sending and receiving units do not match after an update
Bus wiring, connector or supply fault at the second powertrain controller

U0443.d: U0443 is set when a receiver gets frames from body control module B but rejects their content. The letters B to E come into play when a vehicle spreads body electronics such as lighting, locks, wipers or power distribution over several controllers; module A has U0431, a single BCM U0422, and lost contact with B is U0142.
s: Single comfort or lighting functions unavailable
Code stored as history right after start-up without complaint
c: Software of module B or of the receiver sets the code without a real fault
Loose connector or damaged network wiring at body control module B
Supply or ground problem at body control module B

U0444.d: Body control module C is the third body controller in vehicles with distributed body electronics; U0444 records invalid content in its frames, U0143 lost contact. Ford documents the code: TSB 24-2116 covers 2023 F-150 trucks with the 3.5L PowerBoost hybrid that warn of a trailer brake fault even with no trailer hitched, while the trailer module stores U0444:82, possibly next to U0140:87 and U0143:87.
s: Trailer brake fault message although no trailer is connected
Lost-communication codes for the BCMs stored together with U0444
c: Gateway module software level corrupts or delays forwarded messages
Software of the receiving module (e.g. trailer module) misjudges the data
Supply, ground or connector fault at body control module C

U0445.d: U0445 belongs to body control module D, a fourth controller for body functions that only vehicles with heavily distributed body electronics need. A receiver sets it when D's frames arrive but their content fails range, counter or checksum tests; complete silence from D is U0144.
s: A body function handled by module D works erratically or not at all
Warning messages in the instrument cluster
c: Software of module D or of the receiver not matching after an update
Damaged bus wiring or corroded connector on the branch to module D
Internal fault or poor supply at body control module D

U0446.d: U0446 refers to body control module E, the last letter in the series that starts with U0431 for module A. It is logged by a receiving controller when module E is present on the bus but delivers values or protection fields that cannot be trusted; if E stops sending, U0145 is stored instead.
s: Individual body or comfort functions inoperative
Code present in one or several receiving modules
c: Software of the single reporting module misreads the data of module E
Fault in the network branch or connector leading to module E
Low supply voltage or poor ground at body control module E

U0447.d: As the central gateway, serial data gateway module A links the vehicle networks and forwards messages between them. U0447 means a receiver gets gateway frames with failed protection; for lost contact the code is U0146.
s: Several warning messages in the instrument cluster at once
Adaptive cruise or camera-based assistance unavailable
Check engine light on in vehicles that rate the fault as MIL-relevant
c: Gateway hardware or software fault, update or replacement of the gateway
Receiver software logs the code without a real fault (history entry)
Low battery voltage or poor ground at the gateway during wake-up or power mode changes

U0448.d: U0448 concerns serial data gateway module B, a second gateway that some architectures add next to the central unit to bridge further networks; U0147 is lost contact with it. A receiver stores U0448 when B's frames arrive but alive counter, checksum or message authentication do not match.
s: Warnings from several systems at the same time
Assistance or comfort functions on the networks behind gateway B unavailable
c: Software level of gateway B not matching the other modules
Supply or ground fault at gateway B
Internal fault in gateway module B

U0449.d: U0449 points at serial data gateway module C; its lost-contact partner is U0148. The receiver logs it when C keeps transmitting, yet the content breaks the rules agreed for that message, for instance a wrong length, a frozen counter or a bad checksum.
s: Several unrelated warnings in the cluster
Functions on one network segment unavailable
c: Gateway C software sends frames in a layout the receiver does not expect
Wiring, termination or connector fault on a network served by gateway C
Low voltage or poor ground at gateway C

U044A.d: U044A covers serial data gateway module D. A receiver records it when D's frames carry implausible values or violate their counter or checksum; if they stop, U0149 is the matching code.
s: Brief assistance unavailable message at start-up
Driver assistance or display functions limited
c: Receiver software (e.g. camera or assistance module) misjudges gateway data at start-up
Software or configuration of gateway D not matching the vehicle
Supply, ground or bus wiring fault at gateway D

U044B.d: A third battery controller, module C, appears where a pack is divided into separately managed sections or a vehicle has more than one battery system. A receiver, typically the hybrid or vehicle controller, sets U044B when C's frames on cell voltages, temperatures, state of charge or contactor status fail validity checks; U014A is lost contact, U0412 and U0413 cover modules A and B.
s: Hybrid or battery system warning
Reduced electric power or range
Functions supplied by the affected battery switched off
c: Software of battery module C not matching the vehicle controller
Faulty cell or temperature sensing inside the pack section managed by C
Bus wiring, connector or 12 V supply fault at module C

U044C.d: U044C covers the module that controls inductive charging of the high-voltage battery: a receiver coil and electronics on the vehicle take energy from a ground pad without a cable and must agree with the charger on alignment, power and battery limits. A receiver such as the battery or vehicle controller stores U044C when the module's frames arrive but hold invalid status or power values; U014B is lost contact.
s: Wireless charging does not start or stops early
Charging system message in the display
c: Poor alignment or disturbed link between vehicle unit and ground pad
Software of the inductive charging module not matching the battery controller
Internal fault or overheating of the inductive charging module

U044D.d: U044D names the generator B control module. Ford uses the A version for its LIN-controlled alternator: in SSM 50737, 2021-22 F-150 trucks with the 2.7L EcoBoost warn about the charging system and store U012D and U042E in the PCM because a LIN wire rubs through to ground close to the engine mount on the left.
s: Battery or charging system warning
Low charging voltage under high electrical load
c: Chafed or shorted LIN wire to the second alternator
Faulty voltage regulator of alternator B
Second alternator not configured correctly in the engine computer

U044F.d: U044F is stored when a controller receives data from mirror control module B that it cannot use; U014D is lost contact, U0514 covers module A. Depending on design, mirror modules adjust, fold and heat the exterior mirrors, store memory positions or run an interior mirror with camera display.
s: Mirror adjustment, folding or memory function inoperative
Camera mirror display or automatic dimming unavailable
c: Vehicle configuration does not match the fitted mirror modules
Damaged wiring in the door hinge area or loose mirror connector
Internal fault of mirror control module B, often after water entry

U0451.d: U0451 is the code for serial data gateway module E, the fifth gateway letter; lost communication with it is U0150. It is logged by a receiver that still hears E but finds its data implausible or its protection fields wrong.
s: Code stored without noticeable fault
Warnings from systems on the networks behind gateway E
c: Receiver software stores the code sporadically without a real fault
Software level of gateway E not matching after an update
Bus wiring, supply or ground fault at gateway E

U0452.d: The restraints control module decides on airbag and belt tensioner deployment; in many GM vehicles it also sends yaw rate, lateral and longitudinal acceleration and post-crash data to other units. U0452 means a receiver rejects these frames; U0151 is lost contact.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Emergency call or crash notification message
Adaptive cruise or stability functions unavailable
c: Restraints control module software needs reprogramming
Receiver stores the code as history after start-up or network wake-up without a real fault
High CAN bus load, poor ground or connector fault on the restraints network branch

U0453.d: U0453 concerns a side restraints control module for the left side, used where side impact sensing or the firing of side and curtain airbags is handled by a separate unit next to the main restraints module. A receiver, usually the main restraints module, sets U0453 when the left unit's crash or status data are invalid; U0152 is lost contact, U0454 covers the right side.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side or curtain airbag on the left possibly not available
c: Loose or corroded connector of the left side unit, for example under the seat or in the B-pillar
Software or configuration of the left unit not matching the main restraints module
Internal fault of the left side restraints unit, often after a side impact

U0454.d: U0454 is the right-hand counterpart of U0453. Where a separate side restraints unit on the right evaluates side impact sensing or fires the right side and curtain airbags, a partner, normally the central airbag controller, stores U0454 when it judges that unit's messages corrupt or implausible.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side or curtain airbag on the right possibly unavailable
c: Loose or corroded plug of the right side unit, for example under the right seat or in the B-pillar
Software or configuration of the right unit not matching the central airbag controller, often after a module swap
Internal fault of the right side restraints unit, for instance after a side impact on the right

U0455.d: The occupant classification module reads sensors in the front passenger seat and reports to the restraints controller if the seat is vacant, occupied by a child seat or by an adult; FMVSS 208 lets carmakers switch the passenger airbag off automatically on that basis. U0455 means the restraints controller still receives this classification but finds it invalid, whereas U0154 is total loss of contact.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag on/off indicator wrong or flashing
Emergency call function reported as unavailable
c: Restraints controller software needing an update and as-built configuration
Damaged or unplugged seat harness of the passenger seat, for example after seat removal or adjustment
Faulty occupant classification module or seat sensor mat

U0456.d: U0456 means a module receives messages from the coolant temperature control module but rejects them as invalid; U0116 is the lost-contact twin. Such a controller runs electronically managed cooling, for example an electric coolant pump whose built-in electronics, as Bosch describes for its PAD2 pump, take speed commands over PWM or LIN and report back.
s: Engine or coolant temperature warning
Reduced engine power as protection
Check engine lamp on some models
c: Coolant in the plug or pigtail of the electric water pump
Blown fuse or weak supply of the pump or cooling control module
Faulty electronics of the electric coolant pump or cooling module

U0457.d: Information center A is the first of two driver information displays defined alongside the instrument cluster, in practice often the central screen or head unit of the infotainment system. U0457 is stored when a listener still hears this display but rejects what it sends, for example because a message counter or checksum fails, the kind of protection AUTOSAR specifies for safety-related frames; a silent display gives
s: Central display showing wrong, frozen or no content
Network malfunction message in the cluster
c: Software fault or version mismatch in the display or head unit
Poorly seated fuse or weak supply of the display unit
Connector or bus wiring fault at the display

U0458.d: U0458 covers the second driver information display, information center B, which J2012 keeps apart from center A, the instrument cluster and the head-up display; which physical screen a maker calls B, for example a passenger or rear-seat display, is its own decision. A receiving module logs the code when frames from B arrive but fail plausibility, such as a stuck alive counter or a wrong CRC as described in the AUTOSA
s: Second display blank, frozen or showing wrong values
Functions operated through that display unavailable
c: Software fault or unsuitable software level in display B
Loose connector or damaged bus wiring to display B

U0459.d: The head-up display shows speed, route arrows or warnings as a virtual image in the windscreen. It takes most content from other modules and reports its own state, such as brightness, image position, page or standby, back over the vehicle bus or a LIN link to the cluster.
s: Head-up display blank or frozen
Brightness, position or page settings have no effect
c: Software of the cluster or HUD handling messages badly, for example around standby
HUD shutting down or sending fault status because of heat
Connector or LIN/bus wiring fault at the HUD

U045A.d: Parking assist module A evaluates the ultrasonic sensors and in newer cars requests steering or braking for automated parking. U045A flags invalid data from it; U0159 is lost contact, U0544 covers module B.
s: Park assist or automatic parking unavailable
Parking sensor indicator flashing or false obstacle warnings
Emergency braking or collision warning message
c: Parking assist module software needing an update
Water or corrosion in ultrasonic sensor plugs or the bumper harness
Receiver storing the code as harmless history after a software change

U045B.d: ABS module B is a second brake controller, found where braking has to survive a single fault. Bosch pairs an electromechanical booster or its integrated power brake with ESP for that purpose and, for automated driving, adds a separate redundant brake unit; its 2018 show message was that automated driving needs redundancy.
s: Brake system or ABS warning
Automated or hands-off driving functions unavailable
c: Software levels of brake module A and B or the automation computer not matching
Weak supply or ground of brake module B
Internal fault of brake module B

U045C.d: Power steering module B is the second controller of a redundant electric steering system. Bosch presented a fail-operational EPS for highly automated driving in 2017: if one path fails, the system can still steer the car to a safe stop or spare the driver a sudden rise in steering effort.
s: Steering system warning
Lane centring or automated steering unavailable
Steering assist reduced in some cases
c: Software or calibration of steering module B not matching module A
Voltage dips or poor ground at the second steering path
Internal fault of steering module B

U045D.d: Automated driving system control module A is a computer that merges radar and camera data and plans braking and steering for features such as adaptive cruise, lane centring and emergency braking. U045D means a partner hears it but gets implausible content; U015C is lost contact.
s: Automatic emergency braking unavailable message
MIL on in affected Stellantis models
Adaptive cruise and lane centring disabled
c: Outdated software in the front long-range radar or ADAS module
Strained or badly routed Ethernet cable with poor pin contact at the ADAS modules
Internal fault of the ADAS control module

U045E.d: Control module B is the second unit of a split automated driving computer, and the two halves check each other. Stellantis documents U045E in STAR case S2508000095 for 2024-26 Jeep Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer: the CADM and the global navigation and motion module store U045E-00 next to U015D-00, Ethernet link errors and time synchronisation faults, and the freeze-frame data name failed message checks on two internal p
s: Blind spot alert unavailable message
Blind spot lamps in the mirrors stay lit
Driver assistance features disabled
c: Ethernet cable routed too tight, straining plugs and pins at the ADAS modules
Harness clip at the ADAS decision module outside the specified distance
Internal fault of ADAS control module B

U045F.d: Interface module A sits between an automated driving computer and the base vehicle: it turns the computer's steering, braking and propulsion requests into commands the vehicle's own controllers accept and reports their state back. Bosch places this act layer at the end of its sense-think-act chain.
s: Automated driving or advanced assistance refuses to engage
Takeover request or warning to the driver
c: Software of interface module A not matching the automation computer or actuator controllers
Connector, bus wiring or supply fault at interface A
Internal fault of interface module A

U0460.d: Interface module B is the second, redundant link between an automated driving computer and the brakes, steering and propulsion. Bosch says plainly that automated driving is impossible without redundancy, which is why it doubles brake and steering paths.
s: Automated driving unavailable or takeover request
Assistance functions limited
c: Software level of interface module B not matching after an update
Loose plug or supply dips at interface B
Internal fault of interface module B

U0461.d: The audible alert control module produces warning chimes, for an unfastened belt, an open door or lights left on; in GM's list of U codes for the 2011 Saab 9-5 the matching node is called chime alarm control module. U0461 is stored when a partner, often the body controller or instrument cluster that requests or confirms the tones, receives status frames from this module that fail plausibility; U0160 is complete silen
s: Warning chimes missing, wrong or sounding constantly
Belt reminder without sound
c: Software of the chime module or requesting unit not matching
Loose plug or weak supply of the chime module
Internal fault of the audible alert module

U0462.d: The compass module measures the earth's magnetic field, usually with two perpendicular sensors in the interior mirror or overhead console, and sends the heading to a display or navigation unit. Gentex patented a mirror compass of this kind with automatic calibration, compensation for magnetic disturbances inside the car and a link to the vehicle bus.
s: Compass display shows dashes or wrong heading
Heading jumps while driving
c: Compass calibration lost or disturbed by magnetic influences, for example after a battery change or roof-mounted accessories
Loose plug at the interior mirror or overhead console
Internal fault of the compass module or mirror electronics

U0463.d: The navigation display module is the screen part of a navigation head unit that shows maps and route guidance. U0463 marks invalid data from it, while U0162 means it is silent and U0464 concerns the navigation control unit.
s: Navigation map or screen blank or frozen
Warnings of systems that share data with the head unit
c: Software fault or mismatch in the head unit or display
Fuse, relay or supply problem of the display unit
Connector or bus wiring fault at the display

U0464.d: U0464 is stored when a module still hears the navigation control module but rejects its content: a frame whose checksum fails, a message counter that no longer advances, or position, heading and route values outside their defined range. Typical listeners are the instrument cluster or head-up display, which repeat turn arrows, and on some cars predictive cruise or shift logic that reads the map ahead.
s: Turn arrows missing in the cluster or head-up display
Vehicle position on the map jumps or is wrong
Route guidance stops or restarts unexpectedly
c: Navigation unit software or map update fault sending implausible values
Loose connector or damaged bus wiring at the navigation unit or head unit
Weak 12 V battery or voltage dips during start-up corrupting frames
Internal fault in the navigation control module

U0465.d: U0465 flags implausible data from the power take-off (PTO) controller. That unit switches in an engine-driven output for dump beds, aerial lifts or pumps and asks the engine for a working speed.
s: PTO cannot be engaged or disengages on its own
Working engine speed for the body equipment is not held
PTO warning or message in the cluster
c: Damaged or corroded wiring and connectors of the body-mounted PTO module
Mismatched configuration after installing or changing the body equipment
Voltage drops while the PTO and hydraulic loads are running
Internal fault in the PTO control module

U0466.d: U0466 concerns the rear HVAC control module, the second climate controller in vans, minivans and large SUVs that runs its own blower, blend flaps and often a separate control panel for the back rows. A receiver such as the front climate unit or the body controller sets the code when the rear module's frames carry bad checksums, stalled counters or settings it cannot accept.
s: Rear climate controls do not respond
Rear blower or temperature stuck at one setting
Climate warning or fault message in the display
c: Loose or corroded connector at the rear HVAC module, often in the rear trim or headliner
Software mismatch after replacing or programming one of the climate modules
Weak battery or voltage dips at the module
Internal fault in the rear HVAC control module

U0467.d: U0467 belongs to diesels that use a fuel-borne catalyst. A separate fuel additive control module meters a metal-based additive from its own reservoir into the fuel after refuelling, so that soot trapped in the particulate filter ignites at about 350-450 °C instead of above 600 °C.
s: Check engine lamp or particulate filter warning
Regeneration becomes more frequent or incomplete
Reduced engine power once the filter loads up
c: Corroded connector or damaged wiring at the additive pump module near the tank
Faulty additive level sensor feeding implausible values into the module
Module not adapted after refilling the additive or replacing the particulate filter
Internal fault in the fuel additive control module

U0468.d: U0468 marks invalid data from the fuel cell control module, the master controller of a hydrogen car, managing air and hydrogen supply, heat and water in the stack and the split of electrical power between stack, buffer battery and drive. Partners such as the motor inverter, battery management or the hydrogen storage unit reject its frames when checksums, counters or power requests do not hold up.
s: Fuel cell system warning in the cluster
Reduced power, driving on the buffer battery only
Vehicle does not reach READY
c: Fuel cell control unit software needing an update from the manufacturer
Weak 12 V battery or poor ground disturbing the controller
Connector or bus wiring fault between the fuel cell unit and its partners
Internal fault in the fuel cell control module

U0469.d: U0469 means the engine controller or gateway receives data from the starter/generator control module but cannot trust it. On 48 V mild hybrids this electronics sits in the belt starter generator, which cranks the engine, recuperates and charges both networks.
s: Electrical system fault message and yellow or red battery symbol
Start-stop and recuperation no longer work
12 V battery not charged while driving
c: Outdated software in the starter/generator control module
Other CAN or sensor faults disturbing the hybrid bus, with the generator only reporting the effect
48 V battery or 12 V supply problem upsetting the generator electronics
Internal hardware fault in the belt starter generator

U046A.d: U046A is logged when a module, usually the body controller or the overhead console, gets data from the sunroof control module that fails its checks: position and motion reports that contradict each other, a counter that stops changing or a bad checksum. The sunroof module drives the glass panel and sun blind and tracks their end positions.
s: Sunroof does not open or close with its switch
Convenience closing by key or rain sensor no longer works
Panel stops midway or reverses unexpectedly
c: Water in the roof module or its connector from blocked sunroof drains
Lost end-position learning after battery disconnection or panel work
Chafed wiring or loose connector in the headliner
Internal fault in the sunroof control module

U046B.d: U046B indicates that position, speed or time data from the global positioning system module fail plausibility in a receiving unit: a corrupt frame, a counter that stalls, or coordinates that cannot match the movement the car measures through its wheel speeds. The receiver feeds navigation, telematics, emergency call and map-based assistance.
s: Vehicle position on the map is wrong, jumps or freezes
Connected services or emergency call show no location
Clock or time zone set incorrectly
c: Damaged GPS antenna, cable or connector giving poor or jumping fixes
Software fault in the GPS or telematics module
Low battery voltage or poor ground at the module
Internal fault in the GPS module

U046C.d: U046C means that the electric A/C compressor's controller, i.e. the inverter spinning the high-voltage compressor in hybrids and EVs, sends data a receiver refuses: speed, power draw or status with bad checksums, frozen counters or values outside their range.
s: Air conditioning blows warm or switches off intermittently
Battery cooling limited, slower DC charging in hot weather
Climate or hybrid system warning in the cluster
c: Damaged or chafed low-voltage harness or connector at the electric compressor
Compressor inverter software fault or mismatch after service
Weak 12 V supply disturbing the compressor electronics
Internal fault in the compressor control electronics

U046D.d: U046D is about module B, the second of two fuel pump drivers, used on vehicles with two in-tank pumps or a saddle tank; for module A the matching code is U0410. A receiver, normally the engine controller, logs it when the module's reports, such as delivered pump output or its own fault status, arrive corrupt or implausible.
s: Check engine lamp on
Hesitation or power loss under heavy load
Long cranking or stalling
c: Poor ground or corroded connector at the second fuel pump driver
Damaged feedback or bus wiring between pump module B and the engine controller
Worn pump B drawing excess current and upsetting the driver's reports
Internal fault in fuel pump control module B

U046E.d: U046E points to the B unit among exhaust gas sensor modules, a second smart device that warms a probe in the exhaust, interprets its signal, typically from a wide-band oxygen or NOx sensor, and transmits readings and readiness as bus data. The engine or aftertreatment controller sets it when frames still arrive but fail checksum or counter tests, or values such as NOx level or the ready flag are not credible.
s: Check engine lamp on
Exhaust aftertreatment or emission warning
Higher fuel or urea consumption from substitute values
c: Heat-damaged or corroded connector and harness at the sensor module
Aged or contaminated probe making the module report implausible values
Calibration mismatch after replacing the sensor module
Internal electronics fault in exhaust gas sensor module B

U0471.d: U0471 is logged when the airbag controller still receives telegrams from restraints sensor A but rejects their content, for example because of a parity error, a reading outside the sensor's range or values that contradict the other crash sensors. Lost contact would be U0170.
s: Airbag warning lamp stays on
Fault code stored in the restraints control module, sometimes with an internal sensor code
c: Water or corrosion at the connector of a front satellite sensor in the engine bay
Sensor or its bracket deformed by a minor frontal impact
Replacement sensor of the wrong part number or orientation fitted

U0472.d: U0472 points to restraints sensor B: the airbag controller hears it but discards the transmitted values as corrupt or implausible, whereas U0171 would mean silence. Chrysler's NHTSA filing PE11-019 lists sensor B as the right-hand up-front satellite measuring acceleration on its 2007-2008 Jeep models, paired with internal fault B1B71.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal crash detection possibly degraded until repair
c: Front sensor not tightened to specification or loosened after body repair
Chafed or corroded harness between front sensor and airbag controller
Measuring element of the right front satellite defective

U0473.d: U0473 means the restraints controller receives sensor C but cannot use what it sends. In Chrysler's lists from investigation PE11-019, C is the first left-side satellite acceleration sensor, present already on the four-sensor Wrangler JK; its internal fault is B1B72, while U0172 covers lost contact.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side and curtain airbag readiness uncertain
c: Sensor wire pinched or chafed under the B-pillar or sill trim
Side sensor loose because a stud, nut or screw is missing
Sensor damaged by a previous side impact

U0474.d: U0474 flags unusable data from restraints sensor D. Chrysler's lists in NHTSA file PE11-019 assign D to the second left-side satellite acceleration sensor (internal fault B1B73, lost contact U0173).
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side impact sensing on the left reduced
c: Cracked solder joint inside the satellite sensor
Connector or wiring fault at the rear side sensor behind the pillar trim
Restraints controller configured for a different sensor layout

U0475.d: U0475 reports corrupt or implausible data from restraints sensor E; U0174 would be the lost-contact code. No manufacturer publicly ties letter E to a mounting point.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller only
c: Damaged two-wire sensor line or connector
Internal fault in the satellite sensor itself
Restraints controller coding does not match the installed sensors

U0476.d: U0476 is stored when restraints sensor F still reports but its values fail the receiver's checks. Chrysler's lists in NHTSA investigation PE11-019 make F the first right-side satellite acceleration sensor, fitted even to the four-sensor Wrangler JK; internal fault B1B75, lost contact U0175.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side and curtain airbag readiness uncertain
c: Wiring or connector fault at the right side sensor under the pillar or sill trim
Right side sensor damaged or misaligned after a side impact or body repair
Internal fault in the satellite sensor

U0477.d: U0477 concerns restraints sensor G, whose messages arrive but are judged invalid; U0176 is lost contact. In Chrysler's lists from NHTSA investigation PE11-019, G names the second satellite on the right flank, an acceleration sensor with internal fault B1B76, and appears only on the six-sensor Compass and Patriot.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear side impact sensing reduced
c: Sensor of an unsuitable part number installed
Trapped or chafed sensor line causing corrupted telegrams
Sensor reporting values outside its measuring range

U0478.d: U0478 flags invalid data from restraints sensor H, the counterpart of lost-contact code U0177. No manufacturer publishes which sensor carries the letter H; the Chrysler fault tables filed with NHTSA under PE11-019 stop at G.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code present only in the restraints controller
c: Moisture or a damaged seal affecting a door-mounted pressure sensor
Sensor line damaged, for example in a door hinge harness
Restraints controller coded for a sensor set that is not fitted

U0479.d: U0479 records that restraints sensor I sends data the airbag controller refuses; U0178 would be silence. No public source assigns the letter I to a mounting point, and a ninth peripheral sensor is rarely documented.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller
c: Damaged line or connector to the sensor
Sensor disturbed by loose cargo or a poor mounting location

U047A.d: U047A means the airbag controller receives restraints sensor J but its content fails validation; lost contact is U0179. Which component carries the letter J is not published anywhere.
s: Airbag or pedestrian protection warning shown
Code stored in the restraints controller
c: Bumper-mounted sensor damaged by a parking knock or bumper repair
Line or connector fault on the sensor circuit
Controller coding does not match the fitted sensors

U047B.d: U047B: restraints sensor K is heard but its values are rejected; U017A covers lost contact. No manufacturer documents the letter K publicly, so its position stays open.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller
c: Corroded or loose connector in the sensor line
Restraints controller software evaluating the sensor incorrectly

U047C.d: U047C sets when restraints sensor L still communicates but delivers unusable data; U017B is the lost-contact partner. L is the twelfth sensor letter, and twelve is exactly the number of PSI5 sensor interfaces Bosch quotes for its standard airbag control unit; more requires the premium version.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller
c: Damaged shielding or twisted pair causing checksum errors
Controller coding not matching the sensor equipment

U047D.d: U047D reports invalid data from restraints sensor M; U017C is lost contact. A thirteenth satellite exceeds the twelve sensor interfaces of Bosch's standard airbag control unit, so a system using M needs a larger controller such as Bosch's AB premium with up to 18.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller
c: Sensor variant not matching the vehicle configuration
Restraints controller software misinterpreting the sensor data

U047E.d: U047E closes the sensor series: restraints sensor N still sends, but its data are rejected; U017D is lost contact, and the following codes U047F and U0480 move on to belt pretensioner modules. Fourteen external sensors is precisely the maximum Bosch states for its airbag control unit for commercial vehicles.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller
c: Corroded connector or damaged line to the sensor
Outdated restraints controller software or wrong sensor configuration

U047F.d: U047F concerns seat belt pretensioner module A, a belt retractor with its own motor and electronics rather than a purely pyrotechnic tensioner fired by the airbag unit. Such reversible retractors take up slack before a possible crash, during emergency braking or evasive steering, and can warn by pulsing the strap, as ZF LIFETEC describes for its ACR8.
s: Warning that proactive occupant protection is faulty
No belt pre-tensioning during hard braking
Airbag or restraint warning possible
c: Software fault in the belt pretensioner module or its bus partner
Supply or bus wiring fault at the retractor in the B-pillar or seat
Internal fault in the motorised retractor module

U0480.d: U0480 mirrors U047F for seat belt pretensioner module B: the receiver gets its messages but finds them invalid, whereas U017F would mean silence. Honda's patent US 7,686,118 shows how such a unit is tied in: a dedicated electric belt controller drives the retractor motor, sits on the vehicle LAN, takes collision warnings from the brake control unit and receives the buckle signal routed through the airbag controller.
s: Belt pre-tensioning or haptic belt warning unavailable
Restraint system warning message
c: Software fault in pretensioner module B or the unit sending it data
Faulty input relayed through the module, such as the buckle signal
Internal fault in the motorised retractor

U0481.d: U0481 means a module still receives frames from the automatic lighting control module but refuses their content, for instance an ambient-light value outside its range, a frozen message counter or a failed checksum; silence from that unit would be U0180. The unit decides from a light sensor, often housed with the rain sensor behind the windscreen, when the headlamps come on.
s: Automatic headlamp function unavailable, lights must be switched manually
Exterior lighting warning or message in the cluster
c: Light or rain/light sensor delivering values outside its range, e.g. after heat soak or windscreen replacement
Software or configuration of the lighting module not matching the receiving module
Corroded or loose connector on the bus line to the module

U0482.d: U0482 is stored when messages from headlamp leveling control module A arrive but fail the receiver's integrity or plausibility checks; complete loss of contact is U0181, and U048B covers a second leveling unit. Such a module takes axle ride-height signals and moves the beam actuators so that a loaded boot or hard braking does not lift the cut-off line, as Hella explains; dynamic versions also react to acceleration.
s: Headlamp leveling warning in the cluster
Beam height no longer adapts to load and may dazzle or fall short
Inclination display or related functions show fixed values
c: Bent or faulty axle ride-height sensor feeding implausible values into the module
Leveling module software computing or transmitting wrong values
Basic setting of the leveling system not performed after repair or replacement

U0483.d: U0483 means the front lighting control module, which switches low and high beam, daytime running and turn lamps or drives the LED channels in the headlamps, is still on the bus but delivers data the receiver rejects. U0182 would be the silent module, U0484 the rear counterpart.
s: Headlamps or daytime running lamps flicker or flash
Exterior lighting warning in the cluster
Front lamps stay in a fixed default state
c: Weak battery or voltage dips during cranking upsetting the lighting module
Lighting module software or calibration fault
Moisture or corrosion at the module or headlamp connector

U0484.d: U0484 is set when frames from rear lighting control module A are received but carry values the listener cannot accept; U0183 stands for lost contact, while rear module B has U0252 and U0553. Such modules drive tail, stop and turn lamps or LED segments at the back and report their status.
s: Rear light system warning although the lamps may still work
Turn, stop or tail lamp failures not reported or lamps in default mode
c: Software error in the rear lighting module or a module not updated to the current level
Chafed or broken wires in the tailgate or boot lid harness
Water ingress at a rear lamp connector

U0485.d: U0485 means the radio or centre stack still transmits but a receiving module rejects its frames. GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG03B, 25OBDG04B) describe the body control module checking alive rolling counters, protection values, checksums and CRCs of centre-stack signals, among them HVAC control requests: 8 failures in 10 samples, for some signals 14 in 18 or 15 in 16, set it at least 5 s after power-up, with the partial ne
s: Radio resets, black screen or audio sources inoperative
Climate controls on the screen do not respond
MIL on some vehicles
c: Radio or infotainment software level with known message errors, fixed by an update
Radio resetting or waking late so that counters and checksums no longer match
Low supply voltage or a disturbed bus connection to the centre stack

U0486.d: U0486 points to the antenna control module: its frames still arrive, yet the receiver, typically the radio or a keyless-entry controller, discards them as corrupt or implausible. U0185 would mean silence.
s: Poor or no radio, satellite or navigation reception
Remote key does not unlock or works only at short range
c: Water reaching the antenna module through a roof leak or failed fin seal
