Internal fault of the antenna amplifier or module
Damaged coaxial or bus connector between antenna module and receiver

U0487.d: U0487 means the external audio amplifier A keeps sending frames, but the radio or gateway finds their content invalid; once the amplifier vanishes from the bus, U0186 applies, and amplifier B has U0262 and U0563. Amplifiers return status such as mute state, sound settings and diagnostic results to the head unit.
s: No sound or radio muted
Static or crackling from the speakers, sometimes when tapping the dash
c: Backed-out or spread pin in the amplifier or MOST connector
Amplifier software level not matching the head unit
Poor supply or ground at the amplifier

U0488.d: U0488 is logged when the first networked disc drive, module A, still reports on the bus but its data fail the receiver's checks; U0187 would mean the drive is silent, while U0489, U048A and U0491 cover drives B to D. Many GM vehicles of 2013-2015 carried such a separate media disc player with its own fuse: bulletin PIT5344B (ATS, Escalade, Silverado, Tahoe and others) told technicians to cycle that fuse when CD playb
s: CD or DVD playback unavailable
Other audio sources keep working
c: Disc player hung internally, cleared by a power cycle
Poor supply or ground at the disc player

U0489.d: U0489 refers to disc player/changer module B, a second drive in the same network, such as a changer added to a radio that already plays CDs or a DVD unit for the rear seats. The receiver still hears it but rejects the content, whereas loss of contact is U0188; drive A has U0488.
s: Second disc drive does not accept or play discs
Disc error message on the display
c: Replacement changer fitted without removing the transport lock
Mechanical or internal fault in the changer
Vehicle coded for a second drive that is missing or of another type

U048A.d: U048A stands for a third disc player or changer, module C. It is set when that unit's frames reach the receiver but fail its checks; silence would be U0189.
s: Disc playback from that unit unavailable
Code present without any noticeable fault on cars without such a unit
c: Wrong vehicle coding after a retrofit or removal of a disc unit
Supply, ground or bus connection fault at the third drive
Internal fault of the disc unit

U048B.d: U048B concerns the second headlamp leveling control module, B, whose messages reach the receiver but are discarded as corrupt or implausible; if B fell silent, U018A would be logged, while module A has U0482 and U0181. A second address is needed where each headlamp carries its own electronics or a central unit works with lamp-side controllers.
s: Headlamp leveling or adaptive lighting warning
Beam height on one side no longer adjusted
c: Software of the lamp-side or leveling module misjudging actuator feedback
Setup or configuration of the headlamp module not completed after assembly or replacement
Moisture or poor contact at the connector of the second headlamp

U0491.d: U0491 belongs to a fourth networked disc player or changer, module D: frames from that drive still arrive, yet the radio or gateway rejects their content. Its lost-contact partner is U0190; drives A to C have U0488, U0489 and U048A.
s: Discs in that drive cannot be played
Code stored without noticeable fault on cars lacking such a drive
c: Vehicle coding or head-unit software expecting a fourth disc drive that is absent or different
Disc drive D hung up or internally faulty
Poor supply, ground or bus link at the drive

U0492.d: U0492 is set when a television tuner keeps transmitting but the module listening to it, usually the head unit or a display controller, cannot use what arrives, for instance because values lie outside their defined range, a message counter stalls or a checksum is wrong. GM's 2011 code lists for the Saab 9-5 and 9-4X simply call the matching lost-contact code U0191 Television, meaning a separate TV receiver on the bus.
s: No TV picture or a frozen, blurred image
Radio and other media sources keep working
c: Tuner or head-unit software with faulty TV data, cured by an update
Internal fault of the TV tuner
Supply, ground or bus connection fault at the tuner

U0493.d: U0493 covers a personal computer sharing the vehicle network, a slot in the J2012 list that hardly any production car fills. The nearest real case is a fleet or police vehicle with a laptop or mobile data terminal wired into the car: Ford's 2027 Police Interceptor Utility offers an Integrated Computer Screen that mirrors a laptop stowed in the cargo bay, and a Vehicle Integration System that lets upfitters read the J
s: Functions of the connected computer that rely on vehicle data fail
Often no noticeable fault in the vehicle itself
c: Aftermarket computer installation or interface box sending non-conforming frames
Software or configuration of the connected computer
Wiring or connector fault at the vehicle interface

U0494.d: U0494 is stored when digital audio control module A still communicates but supplies data the receiver will not accept. In GM's 2011 Saab 9-5 and 9-4X lists the matching lost-contact code U0193 belongs to the digital radio receiver, at that time the separate XM satellite tuner.
s: Satellite or digital radio channels missing or showing errors
Analogue radio and other sources unaffected
c: Receiver software or activation state producing unexpected values
Supply, ground or bus fault at the receiver's connector

U0495.d: U0495 is the invalid-data code for a second digital audio unit, module B. Where slot A is used at all, it tends to be the digital or satellite radio receiver, as in GM's Saab lists; for B no public code list or bulletin names a concrete device, and no maker documents U0495.
s: One digital audio source unavailable
Often stored together with other network codes
c: Coding or software mismatch about which device occupies slot B
Damaged or pinched bus wiring disturbing several modules
Internal fault of digital audio module B

U0496.d: U0496 points to the subscription entertainment receiver: a tuner whose programmes, typically SiriusXM satellite radio in North America, play only with a paid, activated account. Its frames still reach the radio, but their content fails the checks; complete silence would be U0195.
s: Only preview channels or no satellite channels at all
Terrestrial radio and media work normally
c: Subscription or activation state not refreshed, receiver reports unexpected status
Internal binding failure of the receiver
Supply, ground or bus fault at the receiver

U0497.d: U0497 concerns rear entertainment control module A, which lets people in the back choose media, listen on headphones and watch their own screens independently of the front. It is set when that unit's data reach the head unit or gateway but fail the plausibility, counter or checksum test; U0196 means contact is lost.
s: Rear screens show a rolling or missing picture
Rear headphones or controls without function
Front audio system usually keeps working
c: Software of the rear unit or the head unit mishandling shared video or audio data
Internal fault of the rear entertainment unit or its media player
Supply, ground or bus connection fault at the rear unit

U0498.d: U0498 is logged when the telephone control module, the hands-free or Bluetooth unit, still sends frames but the head unit or body controller rejects their content. For Chrysler the lost-contact partner U0197 is the hands-free phone module (HFM); its bulletins 08-112-14 (2013-2015 Town & Country, Grand Caravan, Wrangler, Challenger and others) and 08-055-17 Rev.
s: Bluetooth pairing or hands-free calls fail
Phone menu unavailable or stuck on a loading message
c: Hands-free module software fault, cured by reprogramming
Module not booting fully or resetting, so its status values are invalid
Internal hardware fault of the telephone module

U0499.d: U0499 means the telematic control module, which carries the cellular modem for remote services and, in the EU, the 112 eCall required by Regulation 2015/758, sends data a receiver rejects. GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG04B) let the object calculation module EOCM3 check ARC, checksum or MAC on the telematics unit's precise positioning frames (heading, latitude, longitude): 6 of 10 faulty, judged over 8 s of a 10 s window, 9
s: Super Cruise or adaptive cruise unavailable on GM vehicles
Connected services or an infotainment service message
Often no noticeable effect, code cannot be cleared
c: Telematics module software sending faulty or unprotected frames, fixed by an update
Corrupted positioning data from the telematics unit (GPS antenna or receiver issues)
Internal fault of the telematics module

U049A.d: U049A reports implausible data from door control module A, usually the driver's door: the unit that runs window lift, lock and mirror and reads the door switches. The body controller or gateway still hears it but rejects the content because a value is undefined, a counter jumps or a checksum fails.
s: Driver window or mirror switches without function
Central locking ignores the driver's door
c: Chafed wires or loose pins in the door harness between body and door
Driver door module internally faulty, for example after water ingress
Wrong configuration or software after module replacement or retrofit

U049B.d: U049B is set when the tachograph still transmits but its data are rejected. In trucks and buses EU Regulation 165/2014 has the device record speed, distance and driving times from a motion sensor, and units such as Continental VDO's DTCO 4.1a pass these values on through two CAN interfaces.
s: Speedometer or tachograph speed missing or erratic
Cruise control, speed limiter or shift behaviour affected
Tachograph fault message
c: Tachograph calibration or parameters not matching the vehicle, e.g. after a tyre or axle change
Faulty motion sensor or sensor wiring producing implausible speed values
Internal fault of the tachograph unit

U049C.d: U049C means the on-board charger, battery charger control module A, is heard on the bus but reports values the battery controller considers invalid. Ford's 2019 OBD summary for hybrid and plug-in vehicles has the BECM set it when the charger's CAN signal shows invalid states for 5 s; U019B is the same charger missing for 5 s.
s: High-voltage battery does not charge, error shown at the charging station
Charge fault message or wrench lamp in the cluster
Driving itself unaffected
c: Charger module software reporting invalid states, cured by reprogramming
Software levels of charger and battery controller not matching
Internal fault of the on-board charger

U049D.d: U049D is logged when a controller, normally the engine control module, still hears from the second glow plug control module but cannot trust what it reports, for instance because a counter, checksum or plug status value is out of line. A second unit is found on diesels that split their glow plugs between two drivers.
s: Check engine or glow plug warning light on
Long cranking or misfire on cold starts
White smoke until the engine warms up
c: Corroded or loose connector or data wire at glow plug module 2
Supply voltage sagging while the glow plugs draw high current
Glow plug control module 2 internally faulty
Module or engine controller software not matched after replacement

U049E.d: Direct ozone reduction (DOR) means a catalytic coating on the radiator, sold by BASF as PremAir, that turns ground-level ozone into oxygen while air flows through the core. CARB grants an emissions credit for it and, under section (e)(14) of 1968.2, wants OBD to watch the coating on cars that claim the credit; a temperature sensor on the radiator serves this purpose.
s: Check engine light on without noticeable drivability change
Emissions inspection failed or readiness not set
c: Damaged connector or wiring near the radiator (impact, corrosion)
Replacement radiator or sensor not matching the original DOR version
Sensor or engine controller software version not matching

U049F.d: The transmission range control module (TRCM) is the shift-by-wire actuator that physically moves the transmission between P, R, N and D after the driver selects a range electronically. U049F is stored by a module that receives TRCM messages whose content it rejects.
s: Shift system or transmission service message
Vehicle stays in Park or does not engage the selected range
Gear indicator disagrees with the selected range
c: TRCM electronics or actuator position sensing faulty
Outdated TRCM calibration (GM 16-NA-373 calls for reprogramming)
Bus wiring or connector fault at the transmission-mounted module
Low or unstable battery voltage while shifting

U04A0.d: Engines with an electric main coolant pump carry a pump whose built-in electronics set the speed on request and send back status and fault information. Rheinmetall, for example, builds such pumps for main engine cooling with a LIN interface and extensive self-diagnosis, and Hella notes that electric pumps can stay off after a cold start so the engine warms faster.
s: Check engine or coolant temperature warning
Engine runs hot or the cooling fan runs continuously
Reduced engine power to protect the engine
c: Pump electronics faulty, often after overheating or coolant ingress
LIN or CAN wire or connector at the pump corroded or loose
Pump running dry or blocked (air in system, debris), reported as error state
Pump or engine controller software not matched after replacement

U04A1.d: U04A1 means the battery management controller keeps receiving messages from interface control module A, one of the slave boards that measure cell voltages and temperatures inside the high-voltage pack, but rejects their content as invalid. Volkswagen names the code: its on-car analysis list of 31 July 2024 for the ID.4 (2021–2024) files U04A1 together with U04A5 and U04A9 under the topic CMCe faults, stored in diagno
s: Electrical system or high-voltage battery warning in the cluster
Reduced drive power
Charging interrupted or refused
c: Software issue in battery management or cell module controllers (VW ID.4 CMCe case, helpline first)
Interface control module A internally faulty
Loose or corroded connector on the pack-internal data link to module A
Weak 12 V battery disturbing the start-up of the battery electronics

U04A2.d: U04A2 covers the second interface board of the high-voltage pack, module B: its frames reach the battery controller but carry implausible content. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning, MIL on plug-in hybrids
Electric range or power reduced
c: Poor contact in the chain connection between interface boards A, B and C
Interface control module B internally faulty
Outdated calibration in the battery controller

U04A3.d: U04A3 concerns interface module C. Such boards do more than measure: they also switch the balancing resistors that bleed charge from individual cells.
s: Hybrid or EV warning, MIL on plug-in hybrids
Power limited, state of charge shown inaccurately
c: Interface control module C faulty (measurement or balancing stage)
Damaged cell sense lead or connector at module C
Interference or contact fault on the pack-internal data link

U04A4.d: Diesel particulate matter (PM) sensors have their own control unit that measures soot on the element and sends the result to the engine controller. GM's 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG04A) check the alive rolling count, protection value and checksum of about twenty soot sensor signals and set U04A4 after 3 bad frames in 10, with battery voltage of at least 11 V for 5 s; it is a Type B code, so the MIL comes on after two trip
s: Check engine light on
Particulate filter monitor not completing, readiness missing
Usually no change in how the engine runs
c: PM sensor control unit or sensing element faulty (heat, soot, moisture)
Replacement sensor of the wrong variant or not yet matched
Damaged wiring or connector between sensor unit and engine controller
Low supply voltage disturbing the sensor unit

U04A5.d: Module E is the fifth interface board in a high-voltage pack, and U04A5 says its data reach the battery controller in a form that fails the checks. This is one of three letters Volkswagen spells out: for the ID.4 of model years 2021 to 2024 the on-car analysis list of July 2024 groups U04A5 with U04A1 and U04A9, all stored in address 8C, and asks dealers to phone the VW helpline before any repair.
s: Electrical system warning message
Drive power or charging limited
c: Software issue in the battery electronics (VW ID.4, clarify with helpline)
Interface control module E internally faulty
Contact fault on the internal link to module E

U04A6.d: U04A6 is set when interface control module F delivers messages the battery controller cannot accept. A board like this checks itself as well: in GM's 16OBDG02 table every interface module, F included, runs four processor performance tests once at each ignition change, for example confirming that its analogue-to-digital converter shows no stuck bits when the input is forced to its limits, Type A after 8 failures in 10
s: Hybrid or EV warning, MIL on plug-in hybrids
Reduced power output
c: Processor or converter fault on interface board F
Contact fault on the internal data link to module F
Supply dropouts of the battery electronics during switch-on

U04A7.d: U04A7 points to interface module G. In a modular battery management system each board sits at a different potential: the ground of the top module can be hundreds of volts above that of the bottom one, so the boards talk through isolated links such as optocouplers or radio.
s: Battery or hybrid system warning
Charging or drive power limited
Fault may come and go with humidity or temperature
c: Moisture or corrosion at internal connectors (leaking pack seal)
Failing isolated communication stage on board G
Interface control module G otherwise defective

U04A8.d: U04A8 is the invalid-data code for interface module H. In GM's 2016 hybrid table 16OBDG02, H is the last of eight boards that the battery systems module reaches through a daisy chain; a pack of that design needs no higher letter.
s: Hybrid system warning, MIL on plug-in hybrids
Reduced propulsion power
c: Interface control module H internally faulty
Connector or lead fault at the last board of the chain
Faulty cell input on board H producing impossible values

U04A9.d: U04A9 refers to interface module I, the ninth position in the series. It is the third of the codes Volkswagen lists for the ID.4: in the dealer analysis list of July 2024, U04A9 appears beside U04A1 and U04A5 as a CMCe fault in address 8C, valid for model years 2021 to 2024, with an electrical system message as the complaint.
s: Electrical system warning message
Charging or power restricted
c: Software issue in the battery electronics (VW ID.4 case)
Interface control module I internally faulty
Contact fault on the pack-internal link to module I

U04AA.d: U04AA flags invalid data from interface module J, the tenth slot. From here on the series only matters for packs with ten or more monitored sections; a nine-module ID.4 battery or an eight-board GM pack like the one in table 16OBDG02 has no J at all.
s: Battery or EV system warning
Power or charging rate reduced
c: Disturbed isolated data link inside the pack

U04AB.d: U04AB means interface module K, the eleventh, delivers data the battery controller judges invalid. What those boards report, cell voltages and temperatures, are exactly the inputs that CARB rule 1968.2, paragraph (e)(15.2.3)(A)(iv), names for monitoring in a hybrid energy storage system; this is why plug-in hybrids light the MIL for such faults, while battery-electric cars, which fall outside these rules, show a batt
s: MIL (plug-in hybrid) or battery warning (EV)
Charging blocked or slowed
Reduced acceleration
c: Faulty temperature or voltage input on board K
Contact fault on the internal data link to module K
Interface control module K internally faulty

U04AC.d: U04AC covers interface module L, the twelfth letter. Twelve is a common pack size: Wikipedia gives twelve modules for the larger ID.4 battery and for the Ultium pack of the Cadillac Lyriq.
s: High-voltage battery warning
Power reduced, possibly no charging
c: Loose plug on the internal link to module L
Fault at the pack's external low-voltage connector

U04AD.d: With U04AD the series reaches module M, the thirteenth interface board, which only exists in packs larger than the common twelve-module layout. One example of such a size is GM's Hummer EV: Wikipedia describes its Ultium battery as 24 modules in two layers that can be switched from parallel to series for 800 V fast charging.
s: Battery system warning
Fast charging slower or refused
c: Corrupted frames on the internal link (counter or checksum errors)
Measurement input on board M reporting impossible values

U04AE.d: U04AE stands for invalid data from interface module N, the fourteenth. Like the other high letters it can only appear on a large pack, and no manufacturer documents it publicly.
s: Battery or EV system warning
Output and charging power limited
c: 12 V supply or low-voltage plug of the pack at fault (check first)
Contact fault on the internal link to module N

U04AF.d: U04AF concerns interface module O, the fifteenth board. In practice a data fault of this kind often follows work on the pack: if a replaced board and the battery controller interpret messages differently, frames arrive formally intact but fail range or counter checks.
s: Battery warning shortly after a battery repair
Reduced power or charging
c: Software levels of replaced board and battery controller do not match
Plug not fully seated after pack repair

U04B0.d: U04B0 closes the series: interface module P is the sixteenth and last letter the code lists provide for these boards, with U01AF for lost contact and U0349 for a software mismatch. Packs with more than sixteen monitored sections do exist, such as Ultium batteries with up to 24 modules, so either several modules share one board or the maker uses its own codes beyond P; which applies is not published.
s: High-voltage system warning
Power and charging limited
c: Contact fault on the internal link to module P
Battery controller software misreading module P

U04B1.d: Despite its place after the high-voltage interface series, U04B1 usually concerns the 12 V side: in GM's 2024 OBD table 24OBDG07 the battery monitor module is the intelligent battery sensor on the 12 V battery, read by the body control module over LIN. GM sets U04B1 when the alive rolling counts of the sensor's signals, among them charged and discharged amp-hours, state of charge, temperature and crank data, are wron
s: Check engine light (GM Type B, after two trips)
Start-stop disabled or charging strategy of the generator changed
c: Body control module configuration lost or mismatched after reprogramming (Alfa Romeo)
Intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal faulty
LIN lead or plug at the battery sensor damaged or corroded

U04B2.d: U04B2 is the B counterpart of U04A4, intended for vehicles that carry a second smart PM sensor, for instance one per exhaust line or one ahead of and one behind a filter. Messages from sensor B still reach the engine controller, but their content is rejected.
s: Check engine light on
Particulate filter readiness not set
c: Control unit or element of PM sensor B damaged by heat, soot or moisture
Wiring or connector of sensor B chafed or corroded
Sensors A and B swapped or wrong variant fitted

U04B3.d: Several hybrid transmissions use planetary gear sets whose shift elements are switched to change the operating mode; two-mode hybrids, for example, combine two extra planetary sets with four clutches to move between electric, power-split and fixed-gear driving. Where a separate module controls such a set and reports its state, U04B3 marks messages from that module that arrive but carry implausible data.
s: Hybrid system or transmission warning
Reduced power or electric-only driving unavailable
c: Planetary gear set control module or its position sensing faulty
Bus wiring or connector at the transmission damaged or oil-soaked
Software of module and hybrid controller not matching

U04B4.d: In hybrid and electric cars, brake blending decides how much of the requested deceleration the drive motor recovers as energy and how much the friction brakes supply; at low speed the hydraulic brakes take over completely. An electromechanical booster such as Bosch's iBooster, paired with a matching ESP, is rated for blending up to about 0.3 g of regenerative deceleration.
s: Brake system or hybrid warning light on
Little or no regenerative braking, shorter range
Brake pedal feels different or harder
c: Blending actuator or its pedal/position sensing faulty
Chassis bus wiring or connector fault
Brake and drive controller software not matching after update or replacement
Low 12 V supply affecting the actuator electronics

U04B5.d: Brake system control module B is a second brake controller. Bosch, for instance, adds a second, redundant brake unit to its Integrated Power Brake on automated vehicles so the car can still be stopped if the main unit fails, and the iBooster plus ESP pairing serves the same purpose.
s: Brake, ABS or stability control warning
Driver assistance or automated driving functions unavailable
c: Brake control module B internally faulty
Chassis or private brake bus wiring or connector fault
Software of the two brake modules not matching after update or replacement
Weak supply on the redundant power path

U04B6.d: An electrically heated catalyst brings the converter to working temperature right after a cold start. Vitesco's EMICAT heater runs at 12, 24 or 48 V and can draw up to 300 A, has been ordered for 48-volt mild hybrid diesel vans with production planned from 2022, and in high-voltage hybrids is fed by a dedicated DC/DC converter.
s: Check engine light on
Catalyst monitor readiness not set
Engine may idle longer at raised speed after cold start
c: Heater control electronics or DC/DC stage faulty
High-current connection to the heater loose or overheated, giving implausible feedback
Bus wiring or connector near the hot exhaust damaged
Module and engine controller software not matching

U04BA.d: A switch input module collects the positions of several buttons and reports them to other control units as network frames. U04BA means that frames from module A keep arriving, but the receiver, usually the body controller, rejects their content: a switch state outside the defined values, a wrong message counter, a failed checksum or an unexpected length.
s: Buttons served by the module inoperative or acting intermittently
Code stored in the body controller without a warning lamp
c: Switch module or receiving controller with incompatible software or coding after repair
Switch input module A internally faulty (moisture, damaged switch contacts)
Corroded connector or chafed data lead corrupting the frames

U04BB.d: U04BB concerns the second switch input module. A receiving controller still hears module B on the bus, but the switch information inside its frames fails the plausibility, counter or checksum test.
s: A group of buttons in one panel not responding
Functions switching on by themselves or not switching off
c: Replacement switch module of the wrong variant or not coded to the vehicle
Switch input module B internally faulty
Loose or corroded plug between satellite and main module

U04BC.d: With a third switch input module, addressing becomes a weak point. Several near-identical switch units often hang on one LIN line as slaves, and each needs its own node address, assigned either by part variant or by an auto-addressing routine at start-up.
s: Buttons of module C ignored while other switch groups work
Button presses assigned to the wrong function
c: Two switch units with the same LIN node address after replacement or failed auto-addressing
Switch input module C internally faulty
Interference on the shared LIN line, e.g. damaged insulation

U04BD.d: With park-by-wire, an electronic unit drives an actuator that pushes the parking pawl into the toothed park wheel on the gearbox output and pulls it out again; there is no mechanical link to the selector. Software holds back engagement until the vehicle has stopped, since the pawl would otherwise ratchet over the teeth.
s: Warning to secure the vehicle or apply the parking brake
Vehicle will not shift out of Park
Park not confirmed on the display
c: Pawl position sensing or actuator inside the module faulty
Bus wiring or connector at the transmission corroded or loose
Weak 12 V battery during park lock actuation
Software or learned values missing after module replacement

U04BE.d: U04BE is logged when a module receives data from battery charger control module B that it cannot accept. Charging hardware can come in more than one stage: the Audi e-tron, for example, was sold in Europe with 11 kW AC charging as standard and 22 kW as an option.
s: AC charging slow, interrupted or impossible
DC fast charging usually still works
Charging fault message
c: On-board charger B internally faulty (Polestar 3 analogy, grid disturbances)
Charger or charging-control software out of date
Bus wiring or plug at the charger damaged

U04BF.d: Some electric and hybrid drivetrains can separate a drive motor from its wheels with a clutch so that an unused axle does not drag the motor along. A Rivian patent describes such a disconnect without a position sensor: the motor speed is brought within a small window of the output speed before engaging, and the control system judges success from how the motor responds to the load.
s: Drive system or all-wheel-drive warning
Reduced power or one motor not used
Clunk or jerk when the motor is coupled
c: Clutch actuator motor or its electronics faulty
Worn or sticking disconnect clutch giving a state that does not match the command
Bus wiring or connector at the drive unit damaged
Software of actuator and drive controller not matching

U04C0.d: The battery management control module behind U04C0 is not always the main controller of the high-voltage battery. Mazda uses the code on the CX-90 (2024–2026) and CX-70 (2025–2026) plug-in hybrids for their backup power unit: the PCM stores U04C0:00, which Mazda describes as an internal malfunction there, often together with P143B, U3008 or U3003 and a lit hybrid system warning.
s: Hybrid system warning light on
Further codes for the backup power supply stored
c: Weak backup sub battery (Mazda CX-90/CX-70 PHEV, AGM YTZ7S)
Battery management or backup power unit internally faulty
Bus wiring or connector fault to the module
